title: Why was there so little traffic from 6 to 7 a.m.?
description: The first bar of the traffic graph is compared with the other five bars to see how small it is, and a reason for it is found by thinking about the hour of the day. The reason is then checked against the next bar of the graph.
teaching_notes: One idea: a graph shows what happened, and we reason about why from what we know of daily life. Watch for answers that only repeat that the bar is short.

video_script.why: The child compares the shortest bar with the others using the scale, and then gives a reason for the small count.
video_script.substitution: Compare the first bar with the other bars, find the gap, and give a reason from daily life.
video_script.anchor: the horizontal bar graph of vehicles passing a busy crossing in Delhi in each hour from six in the morning to noon
video_script.payoff_line: Most people have not yet started for work or school at that hour

final_answer.value: Open-ended: most people have not yet started for work or school at 6-7 a.m.
final_answer.spoken: most people have not yet started for work or school in the hour from six to seven

hold_back: most people have not yet started for work or school
maths_rules: 6-7 a.m. bar is about 150 vehicles, 1.5 units; the other bars are about 600, 700, 800, 1000 and 1200
the next smallest bar is about 600, and 4 x 150 = 600, so it is four times the first bar
the gap with the busiest hour is 1200 - 150 = 1050 vehicles
check: the 7-8 a.m. bar jumps from about 150 to 1200
video_script.design: One idea: read the gap from the graph, then give a reason from daily life and check it against the next bar. The graph stays on the board all video. The reason is open-ended, so the video gives one good reason and says so.
open_questions: The question is open-ended. The video gives the worklist's example reason and does not claim it is the only one.

narration: <bookmark mark='clock'/>Step three, think about the time of day, because traffic follows people. At six in the morning, many are still at home.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Offices and schools open a little later, so few people are on the road yet.
